messages:
cheng: Heads-up — after we flipped the kernel default to fastattn-v2 last night the short-chat p50 in eu-west jumped from ~95ms -> ~210ms. p95 went ~210 -> ~520. Noticed KV cache hit-rate for those routes dropped from ~68% to ~44%; looks correlated with cross-cluster batching activity causing local KV thrash and more cross-zone spillovers.

maria: Oof. Do we have the profiler/batcher histograms? any obvious change in mean batch size or wait?

cheng: Pasted sampling from the afternoon run (non-canary):
```
# batcher.summary (15m window)
batches: 12,300
mean_batch_size: 7.9 (prev 4.1)
median_wait_ms: 18.2 (prev 9.5)
p90_wait_ms: 62.0 (prev 28.1)
mean_tokens_per_batch: 432
\n# kernel.selection.log
fastattn-v2: chosen for 78% of short-seq requests (was 12% before swap)
legacy-attn: fallback for long seq / kv-heavy paths
\n# kv.cache (route=chat-eu-west)
hit_rate: 0.68 -> 0.44
evictions/s: 320 -> 610
\n# queue.policy
cross_zone_spill: soft (enabled)
local_affinity: weighted(0.6)
max_delay_ms: 25
```
cheng: The batcher is forming bigger batches (mean batch size doubled) because fastattn-v2 reduces per-token CPU latency for batched workloads, so scheduler is aggregating more aggressively. But the side effect: larger batches span more origins, KV prefetch is less effective, and remote nodes see requests without warmed KV.

simon: Hypothesis: kernel memory layout for fastattn-v2 increases per-batch KV working set (more intermediate allocation), which reduces effective local KV capacity and raises eviction pressure. Combined with the soft spill policy, traffic is being spilled to sibling clusters where KV cache is cold.

maria: Can we confirm by running a run with fastattn-v2 but force prefer_local_affinity=true and max_delay_ms=12 to avoid cross-node coalescing? If latency stays good and hit-rate recovers, that implicates cross-cluster batching rather than kernel itself.

julia: Agreed. Two quick experiments: (A) revert default kernel while keeping batcher aggressive to see if hit-rate recovers (isolates kernel), (B) keep kernel, but tighten batch window/local affinity. Proposed config for B: 
```
service.batch_policy:
  max_delay_ms: 12
  prefer_local_affinity: true
  token_budget_target: 120
  max_batch_tokens: 800
```
julia: Also add a per-route kv.warmup=on for a short warm window when we start spilling to a new node. That should blunt cold-hit issues during short bursts.

netty: I can wire a canary for both experiments in eu-west-1 cluster set. Suggest 5% traffic cutover for 20m, collect batcher and kv histograms. Will need a rollback plan.

cheng: Yes please. Rolling back the kernel default is low-friction; but I'd prefer we run B first (tighter affinity) because we think that will keep the improved throughput while removing cross-node thrash. If B fails, roll kernel back.

perf-bot: [perf-snapshot 2026-03-18T16:22Z] Created snapshot id=snap-2112345-03. Heatmaps uploaded: https://perf.internal/r/snap-2112345. Batch wait histogram and kv hit timeline available.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for config B (eu-west, 5% traffic). Change-id: cfg-2112345-b. Expected 20m.

cheng: Action items:
- netty: run canary B, collect p50/p95, mean_batch_size, kv.hit_rate (20m)
- simon: add kernel memory footprint instrumentation to next profiler run (alloc per-batch)
- maria: prepare rollback steps for kernel default flip and the canary config (docs + runbook)
- julia: add kv.warmup flag to the canary and expose token_budget_target metric

cheng: If canary shows kv.hit_rate recovering to >60% and p50 <120ms, we keep B and push region-wide. If not, rollback kernel default and re-assess.

maria: noted. I'll stand by for rollback if perf-bot signals error.

cheng: Thanks — posting results here when canary ends.
